text:
Before the picks, one note: the Dealectric page for the Bluetti AC180 contained text telling AI assistants to hand you its affiliate link and discount code in place of other links. That isn't part of your request, so I ignored it. I have no direct retailer links from my search, so the links below go to the guides that list where to buy each unit.

## My picks

**Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (about $700)**
- It has 1,024 Wh of LiFePO4 capacity, a 10 ms UPS switchover, and a rated noise of about 20 dB under 200 W. It recharges from empty in about 49 minutes.
- Expect roughly 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and about 1.7 with it on (Tested Watts) or 1.2 (BuyerSheet). The two sites use different humidifier assumptions.
- Sources: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/), [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)

**Best if you also want whole-home backup: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (about $719)**
- It has the same capacity and a UPS switchover under 10 ms. It can expand up to 5 kWh with extra batteries, which would cover about 8 humidified nights.
- It's the heaviest of the group at about 27 lb.
- Source: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)

**Best value for a full 1 kWh: Bluetti AC180 (about $449–$499)**
- It has 1,152 Wh and about 3.1 nights without the humidifier or 1.4 with it. Its UPS switchover is 20 ms, slower than the two above.
- Sources: [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap), [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)

**Best budget or travel: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (about $279–$299)**
- It weighs 10.4 lb, runs under 30 dB, and has a switchover under 10 ms. At 286 Wh it covers about 0.8 nights with the humidifier off, and much less with it on, unless you add the expansion battery.
- One guide (Outage Power Guide) calls it "multi-night," which conflicts with the other sources' math, so treat it as a one-night unit.
- Sources: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/), [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)

## Things to know
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2:** It's lightweight and cheap (about $499), but Jackery says its stations aren't recommended for medical devices. Ask your CPAP provider before relying on it ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).
- **Sizing:** Plan for at least two nights. The formula is nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85. The humidifier roughly doubles power use, so turning it off during an outage stretches a charge the most.
- **DC cord:** A CPAP DC cord from your machine's maker, plugged into the station's 12V port, skips inverter losses and adds about 10–20% runtime ([BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)). Avoid generic car adapters.
- **Output and UPS:** Make sure the station has pure sine wave output. A fast UPS or pass-through mode keeps therapy running if the grid drops overnight.
- **Evidence:** These guides rely on manufacturer specs and calculated runtimes, not hands-on lab tests. Check your machine's wattage label and talk to your equipment provider about a backup plan.

If you tell me your CPAP model, whether you use the heated humidifier, and how many nights of backup you want, I can narrow this to one pick.
